title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-01-30
lineage: SBD > MR > C > DAT > CDR > EAC(secure) > Cool Edit (minor fixes) > CD Wave (retracking) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture with solid performance – razor‑sharp Jerry leads, standout High Time, Easy Wind and a smoking Other One despite a rough Cosmic Charlie cut.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its tight rhythm section, atmospheric ballads like High Time and Easy Wind, and a blazing rendition of The Other One. Recording quality is generally good for an SBD from early ’70, though a few listeners note it isn’t as pristine as later tapes and the transition into Cosmic Charlie feels painful. Overall the performance shines and the historic significance of Tom Constanten’s last night adds extra interest.

ai_rating.rationale: Average user rating is ~4.3, most comments highlight strong musical moments and decent soundboard audio; only minor recording complaints keep the score just below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners describe the sound as great or very good, but a few note it isn’t as clean as later SBD releases and mention a rough cut into Cosmic Charlie.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Set opens with energetic chaos (Casey Jones, Me & My Uncle) then settles into mellow grooves; ballads and blues flow naturally, with a strong second‑half surge culminating in Other One → Cosmic Charlie (the latter transition feels awkward).

band_member_comments.Jerry: Razor‑sharp leads, perfect tone, and atmospheric solos praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten's last show – his playing is a bit muddled but shines on China Cat and High Time.
